strengths: The opening states the scheduling question and explains the 30-minute sample without repeating a slogan.
Each candidate card gives a time, individual availability, and a concise consequence. Thursday’s card makes the shared slot clear.
The selected state identifies the chosen time and offers a confirmation action. The confirmed state says the choice was recorded on this page only and that no invitations were sent.
The footer’s local-demo disclosure supports the result claim without adding another marketing section.
limits: The captures show the supplied states, but cannot verify click behavior or what happens if a visitor selects a slot that excludes teammates.

findings.observation: The cards identify each teammate’s time zone but show only UTC times. The shared Thursday slot falls on Friday at 00:00 in Tokyo, a day change the page does not reveal.
findings.impact: The visitor can see who is marked available but cannot readily judge what the choice means locally for the four teammates.
findings.repair: Add a dated sample week and show each person’s local time and day alongside availability. Recheck all three slots, especially the Tokyo day changes.

findings.observation: “Compare again” appears in the choice panel before any choice has been made, while the comparison is already visible above it.
findings.impact: The secondary action has no clear purpose at that point and weakens the select → confirm sequence.
findings.repair: Remove it from the initial state. If it helps after confirmation, label its purpose clearly, such as “Change choice.”

strengths: The three candidates are easy to compare, and Thursday’s four-of-four result has clear visual emphasis.
The narrow layout preserves readable availability details and a clear selection action for each card.
The selected state uses a checkmark and changed label as well as a border; the confirmed state explicitly says the choice was recorded only on this page and no invitations were sent.
limits: Static captures cannot establish whether selection, confirmation, navigation, keyboard access, or focus behavior works.
No visual reference was supplied for comparison.
